office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Democratic incumbent Davina Duerr, chair of the House Local Government Committee, faces first-time Republican candidate Maggie Wang; Duerr took about three quarters of the primary vote. The race contrasts Duerr's vote for the 2026 tax on income over $1 million with Wang's pledge to stop tax increases and audit state spending.

candidates.summary: Incumbent State Representative since 2019 and chair of the House Local Government Committee, an architect and former Bothell deputy mayor whose record centers housing supply, permitting and growth management.
highlights: Lists seven bills that became law last term, including cheaper affordable-housing construction, faster housing permits and a growth-management loophole fix [S1]
Voted for ESSB 6346, the 2026 tax on income over $1 million that I-645 would repeal, and co-signed a session report calling it a historic step [S3][S6]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the I-2081 parental-rights list [S4]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 9.9% tax on income over $1 million and co-signed a session report praising it as fixing an upside-down tax code.

housing.basis: Housing record centers supply-side measures: streamlining permits, cutting permitting delays (HB 2418) and lowering construction costs, rather than tenant protections.

local-control.basis: Chairs Local Government and passed state-level rules on growth management and local permitting timelines, setting standards for cities.

climate.basis: Lists a bill phasing out super-pollutant refrigerants and is endorsed by Washington Conservation Action; no stated position on carbon pricing.

experience.basis: In office since 2019, committee chair, seven bills enacted last term; opponent has never held office.

social.basis: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates; no statement of her own on reproductive or LGBTQ+ policy.

parental-rights.basis: Voted for ESHB 1296, which modified and narrowed parts of the I-2081 parental-rights list; no campaign statement on the topic.

candidates.summary: First-time Republican candidate and former Redmond restaurant owner running on stopping tax increases, auditing state spending, public safety and parental rights.
highlights: Pledges to "stop new tax increases" and focus on "lower taxes" [S1][S2]
Supports auditing state spending and cutting wasteful programs [S2]
Names parental rights as one of her three priorities; endorsed by the King County Republican Party [S1][S4]

taxes.basis: Pamphlet and website both center lower taxes and a pledge to stop new tax increases.

spending.basis: Supports auditing state spending, cutting wasteful programs and reducing unnecessary spending; opposes 'bureaucratic expansion.'

safety.basis: Supports law enforcement and first responders and 'safer neighborhoods'; no detailed enforcement or prevention proposals.

experience.basis: No prior elected office; running on a small-business background against a seven-year incumbent.

parental-rights.basis: Names parental rights as a core priority and supports 'parental involvement' in schools, without specific notification or opt-out proposals.
